commands.name: message_search
commands.description: Runs any Gmail search and returns the matching rows without opening a message.

args.name: query
args.meaning: Any Gmail search text.

args.name: limit
args.meaning: The most rows to return; one page holds at most 50.

args.name: fields
args.meaning: Row fields to return, as a comma-separated string or a list; adds labels if asked.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": Gmail has no background mode.

example_requests: Search my mail for the invoice
Do I have mail about the Goa trip?
commands.precondition: Safari is signed in to Gmail in a session you set up, with its display language set to English; the program has Accessibility and Automation for System Events.
commands.postcondition: Nothing is changed and no message is opened.

errors.name: ValueError
errors.when: an argument is invalid

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: a compose or reply window holds typed text, or another app came to the front; nothing is changed

errors.name: SignedOut
errors.when: Gmail isn't signed in; the call doesn't try to sign in

errors.name: UnsupportedLanguage
errors.when: Gmail's elements weren't found by their English names

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode isn't "ui", or the command wasn't verified

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared within the timeout

known_gaps: message_get is left out because it wasn't shown reliable, so use message_search or message_list to read rows, which opens nothing.
A message with an empty body can't be found by exact subject, so it raises NotFound and changes nothing.
Read-back in testing used the same browser and page, so it isn't independent of Gmail itself.
Only one page is read, so at most 50 rows come back.

commands.name: message_send
commands.description: Sends a new message to addresses on the allowed list, then reads it back from Sent.

args.name: to
args.meaning: One address or a list of addresses.

args.name: subject
args.meaning: One non-empty line.

args.name: body
args.meaning: The message text; an empty or whitespace-only body is refused before anything else runs, so always give one when you send.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": Gmail has no background mode.

example_requests: Send Sam a note saying I'm running late
Send this summary to my own address
commands.precondition: Safari is signed in to Gmail in a session you set up, with its display language set to English; the program has Accessibility and Automation for System Events. GMAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS lists every recipient.
commands.postcondition: The message was read back from Sent; it can't be taken back.

errors.when: an argument is invalid

errors.name: StateBlocked
errors.when: a compose or reply window holds typed text, or another app came to the front; nothing is changed

errors.name: SignedOut
errors.when: Gmail isn't signed in; the call doesn't try to sign in

errors.name: UnsupportedLanguage
errors.when: Gmail's elements weren't found by their English names

errors.name: NotSupported
errors.when: mode isn't "ui", or the command wasn't verified

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared within the timeout

errors.name: RecipientNotAllowed
errors.when: GMAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS isn't set, or a recipient isn't on it or can't be confirmed; nothing is sent

errors.name: NotConfirmed
errors.when: Send was pressed but the message wasn't read back from Sent; it may have gone out

commands.confirm: Send this message to <to> with the subject <subject>?
known_gaps: On NotConfirmed the message may have gone out, so check Sent before retrying and don't resend automatically.
Empty-body sends are refused with ValueError.
Attachments, CC and BCC aren't supported.
Read-back in testing used the same browser and page, so it isn't independent of Gmail itself.

commands.name: message_reply
commands.description: Replies to a conversation's newest message and reads the reply's own text back, which marks the conversation read.

args.name: match
args.meaning: The message's exact subject.

args.name: body
args.meaning: The reply text; it must not be empty.

args.name: sender
args.meaning: The sender's name as shown in the row, when the same subject exists more than once.

args.name: mode
args.meaning: Must be "ui": Gmail has no background mode.

example_requests: Reply to the invoice email saying thanks
commands.precondition: Safari is signed in to Gmail in a session you set up, with its display language set to English; the program has Accessibility and Automation for System Events. GMAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS lists the reply's recipients.
commands.postcondition: The reply's text was read back in the conversation, which is now marked read; it can't be taken back.

errors.name: UIError
errors.when: a named element never appeared within the timeout

errors.name: NotFound
errors.when: no message has that exact subject, from that sender if given; nothing is changed

errors.name: Ambiguous
errors.when: more than one message matches; nothing is changed

errors.name: RecipientNotAllowed
errors.when: GMAIL_ALLOWED_RECIPIENTS isn't set, or a recipient isn't on it or can't be confirmed; nothing is sent

errors.name: NotConfirmed
errors.when: Send was pressed but the reply's own text wasn't read back; it may have gone out

known_gaps: On NotConfirmed the message may have gone out, so check Sent before retrying and don't resend automatically.
Replying was tested only with Safari closed, another app in front, a message open and a popup open, not from the other eight start states.
A reply form shows names, so a reply-to address that differs behind the same display name can't be seen.
A message with an empty body can't be found by exact subject, so it raises NotFound and changes nothing.
Read-back in testing used the same browser and page, so it isn't independent of Gmail itself.
